pairs.difference: A: sand and ball in related warm tones, green and red stripes slightly muted, purple cap pushed toward magenta. B: sand is a softer gradient, ball panels are pure emerald green and pure red with the spread hue families (5.4) widest of the pair.
pairs.fix: Keep the ball's green and red panels slightly dusty and related to the sand light; keep sand warm and consistent.

pairs.difference: A: loud lime-green slat wall and orange wood, background chroma above the real range. B: the wall falls to a deeper teal-green and the lower shelf goes dark red, so there is more rest. Weak evidence.
pairs.fix: Mute the wall green a little and let the shelf stay a calm mid orange.

pairs.difference: A: almost one hue, a green wall with a pale blue-grey unit, only 2.6 hue families and shadow chroma kept 2.3, well beyond the real range, so shadows are more colorful than the lit areas. B: wall has a yellow-lime bloom and a lavender body, a little more variety, closer to real.
pairs.fix: Make shadows on the unit and wall a neutral, slightly darker blue-grey instead of an intense saturated one.

pairs.difference: A: flat deep-blue water, sand lavender-grey, gold and brown chest. B: cyan gradient with bright glow at top, saturated magenta gem cluster, gold turned to a very pure yellow, 5.2 hue families.
pairs.fix: Use a calmer mid-blue water with no bright cyan glow, and a duller, browner gold.

pairs.difference: A: orange wall and floor with only two hue families (2.15) and a glossy orange-saturated background (0.137). B: background is a muted dark brown, below the real range in chroma. Either could be real; A reads more uniformly pushed to one hue.
pairs.fix: Add a little desaturated variety to the wood and the cap, with neutral cream and dark brown instead of all orange.

pairs.difference: A: crowns on a green wall, red booth kept in natural red with some darker maroon. B: subject chroma 0.1545, at the top of the real range, booth is a bright pure red and the glass is mint-teal, with a softer background.
pairs.fix: Use a slightly deeper, less neon red for the booth, with a darker maroon in its shadows.

pairs.difference: A: crisp gloves in red with dark maroon and a warm wood floor. B: both gloves are very hot pink-red, subject chroma 0.182 versus A's 0.173, both above range, and softer blur on the wood and blue wall.
pairs.fix: Draw gloves in a deeper leather red with darker maroon folds and a crisp, clear wood floor.

pairs.difference: A: fins have yellow-gold with grey shading and violet reflections in the rim. B: flat orange rim with a hot glow, background chroma 0.257 is higher than A's 0.240, and both are over the real range.
pairs.fix: Tone down the purple ring background and give the fin edges a warmer yellow-gold with violet bounce light.

pairs.difference: A: sand, turquoise water, orange wood, red-white ring, a typical anchor-card spread. B: a close crop with 6.3 hue families, teal-dark water, shadow chroma kept only 0.54, so shadows turn grey-dark and extra colors pile in (sand, deep teal, blue, red).
pairs.fix: Use fewer hue families, with turquoise water, orange wood and one red accent only, and keep shadows tinted blue-green.

pairs.difference: A: magenta wall, orange trunk and a cast palm shadow on sand, background chroma 0.214. B: subject chroma 0.1735, a brighter lime-green and more varied palm leaves against pinker spirals, sand paler.
pairs.fix: Make palm leaves a deeper natural green with fewer lime highlights, and the trunk a plain brown-orange.

pairs.difference: A: lavender wall as a soft gradient, tidy 4.2 hue families. B: pure flat violet wall, plus a crisp saturated blue shoe and red book, and the cooler light reads a little cleaner.
pairs.fix: Use a soft gradient lavender wall, with blue shoes and books slightly dusty.

pairs.difference: A: subject chroma 0.176, above range, pure lime slide and bright blue ladder against pink. B: a calmer deeper green slide with muted tones. A is louder.
pairs.fix: Make the slide a deeper, less neon green, and the ladder a softer teal.

pairs.difference: A: flat blue-violet background with just 1.8 hue families, yellow player. B: more violet gradient, white earbuds, red/green dots, 3.1 families. Both have background chroma above real range; B is more varied.
pairs.fix: Keep the violet background simpler and give the player a quieter orange-yellow.

pairs.difference: A: shadow chroma kept 1.6, above the real range, green dark and rich. B: background chroma 0.237 above A's, with bright green and cream. Both are very loud, weak evidence.
pairs.fix: Dial back the neon green and let the envelope shadows be a neutral cream-brown.

pairs.difference: A: wood board, fruits natural, with the plate pale cyan. B: subject chroma 0.170 above the real maximum, wooden background muted at 0.094 below the range so fruit pops against a dull table, oversaturated red and orange.
pairs.fix: Make the fruit colors natural and slightly muted, with a warmer, more colorful wood background.

pairs.difference: A: dark saturated blue door, painterly leaves, plant green in dark shadows. B: cream wall, door brighter and cleaner, orange frame, subject chroma 0.150 near the top of range, hue families 4.5.
pairs.fix: Use a deeper blue door with warm tinted shadows, and fewer bright citrus-green leaves.

pattern: Generated cards push chroma too high in places (loud neon-pure subject or background hue). They also hold too many clean hue families, with pure green, cyan or magenta clusters. Their shadows are either over-rich or turn grey. The pure-hue bias shows most on backgrounds. My picks on this vector are weak; many pairs gave only small differences.
